Institute.title: Connecting research with the needs of the energy transition.
introduction: Since 2011, IRESEN has brought research, expertise and skills together to support Morocco’s energy transition and sustainable development. With its partners, the Institute connects scientific knowledge with the needs of public stakeholders, businesses and territories.
Institute.statement: Connect research with the needs of the energy transition and sustainable development and build, together with our partners, the capabilities needed to develop, test and valorise innovative solutions in pursuit of this ambition.

position.title: Research rooted in Morocco’s needs, open to the world
paragraphs: IRESEN connects scientific and technological advances with national and regional realities. Its work links energy priorities with industrial decarbonisation, competitiveness and resource preservation.
IRESEN informs choices through science and expertise. Defining and implementing public policy remains the responsibility of the competent authorities.

Support programmes, research platforms, laboratories and expert networks provide the means for this contribution. They bring skills together around specific needs, produce knowledge and prepare for its use.

Institute.missionsLabel: An integrated research and innovation model
missionsIntro: Research & Innovation is IRESEN’s core activity, with three missions: Develop, Test and Valorise.
Studies & Expertise, Skills & Capacities and Cooperation & Outreach strengthen and broaden this contribution. They can also directly address specific needs.
These contributions draw on shared capabilities. Their combination depends on the need; it describes neither an organisational chart nor a compulsory pathway.

missions.title: Studies & Expertise
missions.introduction: IRESEN provides the knowledge, data and analysis needed to prepare public, scientific and industrial decisions. This mission helps build a better understanding of technological options and their application conditions in Morocco and the region.

activities.title: Observe and anticipate
activities.description: Monitor scientific and technological developments, analyse trends and identify emerging technologies. Explore possible developments to help stakeholders anticipate needs, opportunities and constraints.

activities.title: Study and assess
activities.description: Conduct strategic, technical and economic studies. Analyse resources and local conditions, compare technologies and scenarios, and assess their risks, opportunities and socioeconomic impacts.

activities.title: Support decisions
activities.description: Conduct opportunity studies, contribute to sector strategies and roadmaps, and mobilise expertise and technical assistance suited to the questions raised.

activities.title: Our contribution
activities.description: Better-understood options and reliable evidence to prepare decisions, making assumptions, application conditions and analytical limits explicit.

missions.title: Research & Innovation
missions.introduction: Produce knowledge, develop and adapt technologies, evaluate their performance and prepare their use in response to Morocco’s needs.

activities.title: Develop
activities.description: Conduct and support applied research and collaborative R&D. Design technologies and prototypes, and advance their scientific and technical maturity.

activities.title: Test
activities.description: Carry out tests, measurements and characterisation. Verify performance, experiment in representative or real conditions, and identify limitations and the adaptations needed for the intended uses.

activities.title: Transfer value
activities.description: Protect results and prepare their maturation towards use. Explore suitable transfer pathways: licensing, startup creation or support towards industrial and commercial adoption, according to the nature of the results and their development stage.

activities.title: Our means of action
activities.description: Research programming, funding and support, alongside the mobilisation of platforms, laboratories and scientific and technical resources.

activities.title: Our contribution
activities.description: Knowledge and technologies progressing towards use. Exchanges between research, experimentation and use help adapt the work and prepare the next steps.

missions.title: Skills & Capacities
missions.introduction: IRESEN helps individuals, teams and stakeholders develop the skills needed to understand, practise, assess and further develop technologies with greater autonomy.

activities.title: Train and pass on knowledge
activities.description: Develop specialised training, training for trainers and learning through research, through doctoral pathways, scientific stays and exchanges of expertise.

activities.title: Support capacity development
activities.description: Encourage the appropriation of technologies, transfer methods and know-how, and strengthen scientific and technical capacities through support and practice.

activities.title: Share knowledge
activities.description: Share good practices, educational resources and results. Make emerging technologies easier to understand through science communication and awareness-raising.

activities.title: Our means of action
activities.description: Training, research pathways, technical support and knowledge-sharing activities, mobilising researchers, experts and platforms as learning environments.

activities.title: Our contribution
activities.description: Know-how built and shared, and stakeholders better prepared to master technologies and use knowledge in their own activities.

missions.title: Cooperation & Outreach
missions.introduction: Bring together partners, expertise and resources; build joint projects and share Morocco’s contributions.

activities.title: Bring together and connect
activities.description: Animate networks, connect stakeholders and help common needs and projects emerge through scientific exchanges and meetings.

activities.title: Build cooperation
activities.description: Develop scientific, industrial and institutional partnerships. Define common objectives and work, support international exchanges and contribute to scientific diplomacy.

activities.title: Mobilise resources
activities.description: Identify and bring together funding, expertise and complementary resources with partners and funders.

activities.title: Promote contributions
activities.description: Share work and results, represent contributions in networks and meetings, and strengthen their recognition in Morocco and internationally.

activities.title: Our contribution
activities.description: Better-connected stakeholders, mobilised resources and concrete cooperation supporting studies, research and skills development.

values.title: Scientific rigour
values.description: Base our work on explicit methods, reliable data and documented results. Explain their conditions of validity and limitations.

values.title: Usefulness
values.description: Start from concrete needs and explore what our analyses, work and know-how help people understand, decide and achieve.

values.title: Cooperation
values.description: Build with partners, bring complementary expertise together and recognise each contribution to shared results.

values.title: Transmission
values.description: Share knowledge and lessons from practice to strengthen skills, autonomy and the capacity to act over time.

values.title: Responsibility
values.description: Distinguish achievements, ongoing work and ambitions. Document how results are used and present economic and environmental effects when established.

ambition.statement: Make IRESEN a reference for scientific and technological excellence in Africa, contributing to technological mastery and turning research and innovation into value and impact for Morocco.
paragraphs: By 2035, IRESEN aims to strengthen the excellence of its capabilities and their relevance to Morocco’s needs.
The intended impact includes knowledge produced, skills developed, technologies mastered and contributions to the country’s choices and transformations.

council-representatives.title: Council and representatives
council-representatives.description: The board of directors Setting direction and monitoring delivery. Chaired by right by the minister responsible for energy or their representative, the board of directors defines IRESEN’s policy and general direction. It monitors programmes and projects, adopts budgets and accounts, approves agreements and partnerships, and oversees the Institute’s management. It draws on scientific expertise and committee work to inform its decisions. It appoints the Director General and evaluates the performance of the executive management. Members of the board of directors The scientific council Informing research priorities and assessing project relevance. Bringing together international clean-technology experts, the scientific council considers Morocco’s needs in the light of scientific advances and technological trajectories. It examines research areas and recommends programme priorities. It assesses the scientific relevance of projects proposed for funding and submits recommendations to the board of directors, which decides on their acceptance and financing. Its expertise supports the quality of the work and its relevance to the national energy transition. needs-challenges.title: Start with needs. Advance solutions.
needs-challenges.description: IRESEN’s R&D roadmap aims to address concrete challenges faced by energy, industry and territorial stakeholders. It directs research towards solutions whose performance can be verified in Moroccan operating conditions, taking account of cost, environmental impact and adoption potential. Seven themes structure this ambition. Each comprises four research axes with objectives and intended benefits. Themes define the challenges; axes specify the questions; programmes organise interventions; projects put them into practice. Develop Overcome scientific and technical barriers to generate knowledge, design methods and develop solutions. Test Test solutions under representative conditions to establish their performance, reliability and limits. Transfer Prepare the use of results with identified beneficiaries by addressing transfer, adoption and industrialisation conditions.

theme-renewables.title: Renewable energy and flexible electricity systems
theme-renewables.description: Produce, integrate and use renewable electricity better. Improve renewable energy performance and integration into the electricity system, accounting for climate, grid constraints and users’ needs. Performance and durability in harsh conditions Understand and reduce the effects of heat, dust, corrosion and ageing. Test water-efficient maintenance and cleaning solutions. Storage and hybridisation across scales Compare and optimise batteries, thermal storage and other solutions according to expected services, storage duration and climate conditions. Active grids and renewable integration Improve forecasting, control and protection of electricity systems and microgrids. Assess their behaviour under production variations and disturbances. Demand flexibility Adapt consumption in industry, water services, buildings and charging to grid constraints without reducing the services provided. More reliable production, better renewable integration, controlled consumption peaks and lower service costs.

theme-hydrogen.title: Renewable hydrogen and derived molecules
theme-hydrogen.description: Connect hydrogen technologies with relevant uses. Study the technical, economic and environmental conditions for producing and using renewable hydrogen and its derivatives. Compare solutions to identify uses where they offer a justified response. Dynamic electrolysis and durability Optimise electrolyser operation under variable renewable supply by studying energy consumption, degradation and availability. Water–energy–hydrogen integration Combine water treatment, desalination where relevant and heat recovery to reduce resource consumption and control discharge impacts. Conversion, storage and logistics Study conversion chains, particularly renewable ammonia, alongside storage and transport, assessing losses, safety and delivered cost. Substitution in priority uses Test relevant industrial applications against fossil solutions and direct electrification. Clarify adoption conditions. Better-controlled production and supply chains, careful use of water and energy, and uses justified by their industrial and environmental value.

theme-industry.title: Resource-efficient industry and low-carbon processes
theme-industry.description: Reduce consumption and emissions, strengthen competitiveness. Develop solutions suited to industrial processes to improve energy performance and reduce emissions. The objective is to demonstrate gains and clarify the conditions for replicating them at other sites. Efficiency and heat recovery Optimise processes and auxiliary equipment. Develop heat recovery and reuse solutions to reduce the energy required for production. Electrification and renewable heat Test heat pumps, electric heating and solar thermal technologies according to process temperatures and constraints. Materials, processes and residual carbon Reduce emissions through formulations and material substitutions. Study carbon dioxide capture, use or storage in justified cases, verifying the complete balance and the fate of the carbon. Industrial performance measurement and optimisation Develop measurement methods, models and verifiable tools to compare solutions, confirm savings and support decisions. Lower energy consumption per product, verifiable emissions reductions and solutions technically and economically suited to industry.

theme-water.title: Water–energy–agriculture nexus and resilience
theme-water.description: Manage water, energy and agricultural needs together. Improve water services and agricultural resilience while controlling energy requirements. Develop solutions suited to arid regions, jointly assessing water use, energy performance and effects on agricultural production. Efficient desalination and treatment Optimise processes, membranes, energy recovery and renewable supply while incorporating water quality and discharge management. Controlled irrigation and pumping Combine crop needs, water monitoring and energy management to improve irrigation without encouraging increased withdrawals. Water reuse and local loops Validate treatment and reuse solutions suited to their uses, accounting for health, agronomic and energy requirements. Agrivoltaics and integrated farming systems Compare arrangements combining farming and photovoltaics to verify effects on crops, water, energy production and land use. Less energy-intensive water services, better water productivity and more resilient farming systems, without shifting pressures onto other resources.

theme-circular.title: Bioenergy and circular resource recovery
theme-circular.description: Recover value from residues and extend equipment life. Produce energy and recover materials from residual resources that can actually be mobilised. Also study repair, reuse and material recovery solutions for energy-transition equipment. Sustainable resource availability and supply chains Identify accessible residues, accounting for seasonality, existing uses, logistics and soil and water constraints. Biogas, biomethane and coproduct recovery Adapt digestion, upgrading and digestate use to available resources, measuring yields and methane leakage. Thermochemical conversion and bio-based products Compare targeted pyrolysis, gasification or product-conversion processes according to markets, costs and environmental performance. Circularity of transition equipment Develop repair, reuse, second-life and material recovery approaches while verifying the performance and safety of the equipment concerned. Recovery suited to available resources, longer service life and environmental benefits established across the lifecycle, without assuming biomass is carbon-neutral.

theme-buildings.title: Resource-efficient and resilient buildings and territories
theme-buildings.description: Maintain comfort and services with less energy. Develop solutions suited to buildings, uses and climate conditions to reduce energy needs. Combine actual performance, affordability and resilience to heat. Bioclimatic envelopes and renovation Test materials, shading, ventilation and assemblies to improve comfort and reduce thermal needs according to building types and climate zones. Cooling and efficient equipment Compare passive and active solutions, their equipment and controls to maintain comfort while managing consumption and electricity peaks. Territorial services and local energy systems Optimise lighting, public buildings and local energy systems by studying shared use, operation and maintenance requirements. Heat resilience and adoption Test solutions for vulnerable sites and understand renovation adoption conditions, accounting for users’ needs and practices. Better comfort, controlled consumption and operating costs, and improved service continuity during severe heat.

theme-mobility.title: Low-carbon mobility and transport infrastructure
theme-mobility.description: Adapt mobility solutions to actual uses. Study electrification and other low-carbon solutions according to transport needs, climate conditions and operating constraints. Assess vehicles, batteries, charging and journey organisation together. Electrification of intensive-use fleets Compare vehicles, sizing and operation for buses, logistics and professional fleets according to use profiles. Managed charging and grid integration Optimise charging locations, power and schedules to provide the service while controlling peaks and grid constraints. Batteries, diagnosis and durability in use Validate thermal management, state-of-health estimation, repair and reuse criteria to extend safe service life. Logistics and choice of modes or energy carriers Compare flow organisation, transport modes and propulsion. Examine hydrogen and derivatives for uses where they are justified. Lower-emission transport services, available fleets, reliable charging and costs suited to users’ needs.

The principle is simple: bring scientific expertise and economic needs together in collaborative projects. Calls define the challenges, participation requirements and forms of support. data-uses.title: Data, purposes and retention
data-uses.description: The Contact form prepares an email in your browser: name, email, subject and message are needed to compose the request; organisation and telephone are optional. The website neither sends nor stores the entered data. You review and send the draft from your own email application. Unless you send it, no message is transmitted to IRESEN.
details: If you send an email, IRESEN receives the information and attachments you choose to provide, to understand and respond to your request. Application processes and contact links also use your email application; the website offers no online submission of applications or personal files. Include only useful information; do not send identity documents or sensitive data without a specific need and appropriate instructions.

Received email is intended for authorised people handling your request. Retention depends on the follow-up needed and applicable obligations; you can request details relevant to your correspondence. The form draft stays in memory until the page is closed or reloaded. The cookie choice is kept for 180 days.

To display pages, the infrastructure receives your IP address and technical connection information. Technical logs may be used for security and troubleshooting. No advertising or audience analytics tool is integrated. The footer newsletter does not register subscriptions. Search terms are sent to the search service to provide results and appear in the URL; avoid entering personal data.

To limit search abuse, a protected fingerprint of the connection address and a counter are kept in a one-minute window. Typed queries and the raw address are not stored in this counter. Expired windows are deleted during subsequent searches; hosting logs and backups follow separate rules to be confirmed with IT.

Roadmap.title: R&D roadmap
Roadmap.tagline: Research rooted in Morocco’s needs, open to the world.
Roadmap.description: Develop, test and transfer innovative energy solutions that are robust and resource-efficient. Our roadmap connects Morocco’s needs with research questions, with the ambition to produce solutions adaptable to other contexts.
introductionParagraphs: IRESEN’s R&D roadmap aims to address concrete challenges faced by energy, industry and territorial stakeholders. It directs research towards solutions whose performance can be verified in Moroccan operating conditions, taking account of cost, environmental impact and adoption potential.

Seven themes structure this ambition. Each comprises four research axes with objectives and intended benefits. Themes define the challenges; axes specify the questions; programmes organise interventions; projects put them into practice.

steps.title: Develop
steps.description: Overcome scientific and technical barriers to generate knowledge, design methods and develop solutions.

steps.title: Test
steps.description: Test solutions under representative conditions to establish their performance, reliability and limits.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.description: Prepare the use of results with identified beneficiaries by addressing transfer, adoption and industrialisation conditions.

Roadmap.collaborationTitle: Turn these priorities into useful projects.
collaborationParagraphs: An industrial need, a territorial challenge, scientific expertise or an experimental setting to share?

Let us build collaborations around concrete questions: develop a solution, verify its performance or prepare its transfer. Users’ needs and partners’ skills give research its relevance and prospects for application.

renewables.title: Renewable energy and flexible electricity systems
renewables.headline: Produce, integrate and use renewable electricity better.
renewables.description: Improve renewable energy performance and integration into the electricity system, accounting for climate, grid constraints and users’ needs.

axes.title: Performance and durability in harsh conditions
axes.description: Understand and reduce the effects of heat, dust, corrosion and ageing. Test water-efficient maintenance and cleaning solutions.

axes.title: Storage and hybridisation across scales
axes.description: Compare and optimise batteries, thermal storage and other solutions according to expected services, storage duration and climate conditions.

axes.title: Active grids and renewable integration
axes.description: Improve forecasting, control and protection of electricity systems and microgrids. Assess their behaviour under production variations and disturbances.

axes.title: Demand flexibility
axes.description: Adapt consumption in industry, water services, buildings and charging to grid constraints without reducing the services provided.

renewables.benefits: More reliable production, better renewable integration, controlled consumption peaks and lower service costs.
renewables.imageAlt: Renewable electricity system: solar panel, wind turbine and storage.

hydrogen.title: Renewable hydrogen and derived molecules
hydrogen.headline: Connect hydrogen technologies with relevant uses.
hydrogen.description: Study the technical, economic and environmental conditions for producing and using renewable hydrogen and its derivatives. Compare solutions to identify uses where they offer a justified response.

axes.title: Dynamic electrolysis and durability
axes.description: Optimise electrolyser operation under variable renewable supply by studying energy consumption, degradation and availability.

axes.title: Water–energy–hydrogen integration
axes.description: Combine water treatment, desalination where relevant and heat recovery to reduce resource consumption and control discharge impacts.

axes.title: Conversion, storage and logistics
axes.description: Study conversion chains, particularly renewable ammonia, alongside storage and transport, assessing losses, safety and delivered cost.

axes.title: Substitution in priority uses
axes.description: Test relevant industrial applications against fossil solutions and direct electrification. Clarify adoption conditions.

hydrogen.benefits: Better-controlled production and supply chains, careful use of water and energy, and uses justified by their industrial and environmental value.

industry.title: Resource-efficient industry and low-carbon processes
industry.headline: Reduce consumption and emissions, strengthen competitiveness.
industry.description: Develop solutions suited to industrial processes to improve energy performance and reduce emissions. The objective is to demonstrate gains and clarify the conditions for replicating them at other sites.

axes.title: Efficiency and heat recovery
axes.description: Optimise processes and auxiliary equipment. Develop heat recovery and reuse solutions to reduce the energy required for production.

axes.title: Electrification and renewable heat
axes.description: Test heat pumps, electric heating and solar thermal technologies according to process temperatures and constraints.

axes.title: Materials, processes and residual carbon
axes.description: Reduce emissions through formulations and material substitutions. Study carbon dioxide capture, use or storage in justified cases, verifying the complete balance and the fate of the carbon.

axes.title: Industrial performance measurement and optimisation
axes.description: Develop measurement methods, models and verifiable tools to compare solutions, confirm savings and support decisions.

industry.benefits: Lower energy consumption per product, verifiable emissions reductions and solutions technically and economically suited to industry.
industry.imageAlt: Industrial processes: heat exchanger, heat pump and thermal circuits.

water.title: Water–energy–agriculture nexus and resilience
water.headline: Manage water, energy and agricultural needs together.
water.description: Improve water services and agricultural resilience while controlling energy requirements. Develop solutions suited to arid regions, jointly assessing water use, energy performance and effects on agricultural production.

axes.title: Efficient desalination and treatment
axes.description: Optimise processes, membranes, energy recovery and renewable supply while incorporating water quality and discharge management.

axes.title: Controlled irrigation and pumping
axes.description: Combine crop needs, water monitoring and energy management to improve irrigation without encouraging increased withdrawals.

axes.title: Water reuse and local loops
axes.description: Validate treatment and reuse solutions suited to their uses, accounting for health, agronomic and energy requirements.

axes.title: Agrivoltaics and integrated farming systems
axes.description: Compare arrangements combining farming and photovoltaics to verify effects on crops, water, energy production and land use.

water.benefits: Less energy-intensive water services, better water productivity and more resilient farming systems, without shifting pressures onto other resources.
water.imageAlt: Agrivoltaic system, irrigation and water management.

circular.title: Bioenergy and circular resource recovery
circular.headline: Recover value from residues and extend equipment life.
circular.description: Produce energy and recover materials from residual resources that can actually be mobilised. Also study repair, reuse and material recovery solutions for energy-transition equipment.

axes.title: Sustainable resource availability and supply chains
axes.description: Identify accessible residues, accounting for seasonality, existing uses, logistics and soil and water constraints.

axes.title: Biogas, biomethane and coproduct recovery
axes.description: Adapt digestion, upgrading and digestate use to available resources, measuring yields and methane leakage.

axes.title: Thermochemical conversion and bio-based products
axes.description: Compare targeted pyrolysis, gasification or product-conversion processes according to markets, costs and environmental performance.

axes.title: Circularity of transition equipment
axes.description: Develop repair, reuse, second-life and material recovery approaches while verifying the performance and safety of the equipment concerned.

circular.benefits: Recovery suited to available resources, longer service life and environmental benefits established across the lifecycle, without assuming biomass is carbon-neutral.
circular.imageAlt: Bioenergy, residual resources and second-life equipment.

buildings.title: Resource-efficient and resilient buildings and territories
buildings.headline: Maintain comfort and services with less energy.
buildings.description: Develop solutions suited to buildings, uses and climate conditions to reduce energy needs. Combine actual performance, affordability and resilience to heat.

axes.title: Bioclimatic envelopes and renovation
axes.description: Test materials, shading, ventilation and assemblies to improve comfort and reduce thermal needs according to building types and climate zones.

axes.title: Cooling and efficient equipment
axes.description: Compare passive and active solutions, their equipment and controls to maintain comfort while managing consumption and electricity peaks.

axes.title: Territorial services and local energy systems
axes.description: Optimise lighting, public buildings and local energy systems by studying shared use, operation and maintenance requirements.

axes.title: Heat resilience and adoption
axes.description: Test solutions for vulnerable sites and understand renovation adoption conditions, accounting for users’ needs and practices.

buildings.benefits: Better comfort, controlled consumption and operating costs, and improved service continuity during severe heat.
buildings.imageAlt: Bioclimatic building with shading, solar roof and planted courtyard.

mobility.title: Low-carbon mobility and transport infrastructure
mobility.headline: Adapt mobility solutions to actual uses.
mobility.description: Study electrification and other low-carbon solutions according to transport needs, climate conditions and operating constraints. Assess vehicles, batteries, charging and journey organisation together.

axes.title: Electrification of intensive-use fleets
axes.description: Compare vehicles, sizing and operation for buses, logistics and professional fleets according to use profiles.

axes.title: Managed charging and grid integration
axes.description: Optimise charging locations, power and schedules to provide the service while controlling peaks and grid constraints.

axes.title: Batteries, diagnosis and durability in use
axes.description: Validate thermal management, state-of-health estimation, repair and reuse criteria to extend safe service life.

axes.title: Logistics and choice of modes or energy carriers
axes.description: Compare flow organisation, transport modes and propulsion. Examine hydrogen and derivatives for uses where they are justified.

mobility.benefits: Lower-emission transport services, available fleets, reliable charging and costs suited to users’ needs.
mobility.imageAlt: Electric bus, managed charging and photovoltaic canopy.

Governance.title: Governance and organisation
Governance.tagline: Connecting national priorities, scientific rigour and delivery.
Governance.introduction: IRESEN’s governance brings together public actors, energy-sector partners and scientific expertise to guide activities and monitor results. Its organisation mobilises the capabilities needed for Research & Innovation, the Institute’s core activity, and the complementary dimensions of Studies & Expertise, Skills & Capacities and Cooperation & Outreach.

mission.title: Governance serving the Institute’s missions
paragraphs: A non-profit association established at the initiative of the State, IRESEN brings together public institutions, businesses and academic stakeholders around research and innovation for the energy transition.

Its governing bodies connect strategic direction, scientific evaluation, monitoring of commitments and management oversight. The State–IRESEN agreement sets out the Institute’s assigned missions, associated resources and objectives to monitor.
This structure connects national needs with research, experimental capabilities and opportunities to use the results.

administration.title: The board of directors
paragraphs: Chaired by right by the minister responsible for energy or their representative, the board of directors defines IRESEN’s policy and general direction. It monitors programmes and projects, adopts budgets and accounts, approves agreements and partnerships, and oversees the Institute’s management.
It draws on scientific expertise and committee work to inform its decisions. It appoints the Director General and evaluates the performance of the executive management.
administration.membersTitle: Members of the board of directors

science.title: The scientific council
science.tagline: Informing research priorities and assessing project relevance.
paragraphs: Bringing together international clean-technology experts, the scientific council considers Morocco’s needs in the light of scientific advances and technological trajectories.

It examines research areas and recommends programme priorities. It assesses the scientific relevance of projects proposed for funding and submits recommendations to the board of directors, which decides on their acceptance and financing.
Its expertise supports the quality of the work and its relevance to the national energy transition.

items.title: The strategy and monitoring committee
items.description: It ensures that IRESEN’s activities remain consistent with the national energy strategy and commitments under the State–IRESEN agreement. It examines action plans, project progress and implementation reports, and proposes adjustments to the competent bodies.

items.title: The audit committee
items.description: It assists the board of directors in reviewing financial information, internal controls and risk management. It analyses audit findings, makes recommendations and monitors corrective measures. Certification of the accounts is the statutory auditor’s responsibility.

items.title: The general assembly
items.description: It brings together the association’s members, approves annual accounts and activity and financial reports, and votes on the provisional budget. It exercises the powers reserved to it by the statutes.

organisation.title: Executive management and three complementary divisions
organisation.description: The executive management implements the decisions of the board of directors. It coordinates scientific, technical, administrative and financial activities, mobilises the necessary resources and reports on progress against programmes and commitments.

contributions.title: An organisation mobilised around IRESEN’s contributions

Programmes, platforms and the expert network mobilise complementary resources according to needs. Partnerships and cooperation connect this work with public, scientific and industrial stakeholders.
Within Research & Innovation, this complementarity makes it possible to develop knowledge and solutions, test their performance and prepare the valorisation of results.

soukaina.name: Soukaina BOUDOUDOU
soukaina.role: Director of R&D&I Programmes and the Expert Network
soukaina.biography:
An electrical engineer with a PhD in electrical engineering, Soukaina BOUDOUDOU is a graduate of the University of Technology of Belfort-Montbéliard and the Mohammadia School of Engineers. Her research focuses on energy management, hybrid electrical systems and microgrids.

Her career includes postdoctoral research on storage combining batteries and supercapacitors. At IRESEN, she evaluated and monitored research projects before taking responsibility for R&D&I programmes and the expert network, connecting scientific expertise, project support and energy-transition challenges.

ayoub.name: Ayoub HIRT
ayoub.role: Director of Platform Development and Structuring Projects
ayoub.biography:
Ayoub HIRT is Director of Platforms Development and Strategic Projects at IRESEN. His career at the Institute includes heading the Green Chemistry, Bioenergy and Agritech Department and research and innovation activities in energy technologies.

His areas of work include green hydrogen, Power-to-X and bioenergy. He contributes to exchanges between scientific, institutional and industrial stakeholders on these sectors, their infrastructure and the skills needed for their development.

mouhcine.name: Mouhcine BENMEZIANE
mouhcine.role: Director of Partnerships and Innovation Marketing
mouhcine.biography:
Mouhcine BENMEZIANE is Director of Partnerships and Innovation Marketing at IRESEN. For more than a decade, he has developed cooperation and connections between research, public institutions and businesses in green technologies. His work at the Institute brings together international cooperation, science communication and technology intelligence.

He works to make research understandable, connect expertise and build partnerships that support innovation. His approach combines an understanding of technology, knowledge sharing and connections between stakeholders to support the energy transition and the international reach of Moroccan research.

He holds a master’s degree in science and technology specialising in industrial management engineering and a bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering. He complements this background with continuing education in science communication, renewable energy and sustainable business strategy, including Harvard Business School Online’s Sustainable Business Strategy programme.

laila.name: Laila TYDRINI
laila.biography:
Laila TYDRINI joined IRESEN in 2012 as an accounting officer. Over the years, her responsibilities expanded to financial management, human resources and the Institute’s administration.

As Administrative Manager, she now oversees a substantial share of support activities: quality, human resources, finance, accounting, preparation of financial statements, administration and legal affairs follow-up. Her career has accompanied the Institute’s organisational development and the changing resources needed by its teams.

imane.name: Imane MOUBACHIR
imane.biography:
Imane MOUBACHIR works in strategy and organisation at IRESEN. Her activities concern translating the Institute’s priorities into action, management tools and improvements to internal operations.

Her work connects institutional priorities, the coordination of activities and the organisation of resources used by the teams.

jamaleddine.name: Jamaleddine FOUHAM
jamaleddine.biography:
Jamaleddine FOUHAM works in information technology and information systems at IRESEN. His remit concerns the operation and development of the Institute’s IT and digital tools.

He supports teams’ uses and the needs of scientific and administrative activities, contributing to the organisation’s daily operations.

intro.title: One network, complementary expertise
paragraphs: IRESEN’s platform network grew from an ambition to build, with its partners, the scientific and technological capabilities needed for the energy transition. Developed notably with Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and the support of national and international partners, it brings research, training and innovation closer to the needs of society and industry.

Each platform offers a complementary specialization and experimental environment. Their network enables shared equipment and teams, combines expertise and studies solutions in different climatic and territorial conditions, in Morocco and across Africa.

Produce knowledge, develop and adapt technologies, evaluate their performance and prepare their use in response to Morocco’s needs. A platform can support research, testing and training. A partnership can bring together expertise and resources for several contributions.

Developed by IRESEN and UM6P with support from Korean cooperation, it brings together construction, energy and digital disciplines.

Designed as a full-scale laboratory, it studies materials, architecture, equipment and uses together. This approach helps design more efficient, comfortable buildings while exploring their interaction with renewable generation, storage and electric mobility.

greenh2a.lead: Prepare industrial applications for green hydrogen
paragraphs: Developed by IRESEN, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and OCP Group, GreenH2A is a platform dedicated to research and innovation in green hydrogen and its Power-to-X applications: converting renewable electricity into hydrogen and added-value molecules.

Its distinctive approach covers the entire value chain, from hydrogen production to conversion and industrial uses. It aims to compare technologies, develop pilots and produce the knowledge needed for skills development and deployment of the sector.

intro.title: Resources to turn research into useful solutions.
paragraphs: Since its creation, IRESEN has acted as an agency of means: mobilising funding and supporting applied research projects led by universities, research centres and businesses.

This mission is now organised through research, development and innovation programmes — R&D&I. Aligned with Morocco’s energy priorities, they give partners a shared framework to develop, test and put innovative solutions to use.

The principle is simple: bring scientific expertise and economic needs together in collaborative projects. Calls define the challenges, participation requirements and forms of support. Selected projects receive funding and guidance tailored to the scheme.

Programmes and funding are instruments of Research & Innovation. IRESEN also draws on internal research, industrial co-development, international scientific cooperation and the adaptation of existing technologies.
